chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If a free man kills a slave, he must pay his value and be disciplined.
It was said to him: Then what if his value is twenty thousand? He said: The value of a slave is not to exceed the blood money of a free person.

key_terms.أُدِّبَ: he is disciplined with punitive chastisement
key_terms.الْحُرُّ: a free person, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: a slave; the victim discussed in the ruling
key_terms.دِيَةِ حُرٍّ: the blood money payable for a free person
key_terms.قِيمَتَهُ: his monetary value or assessed price

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a free man kills a slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a free person who kills a slave: he is liable for the slave's financial value and is also subject to disciplinary punishment. It further establishes that the assessed value payable for the slave does not exceed the diyah of a free person, even if the market value is higher.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5268 - Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"If a free man kills a slave, he must pay the slave's value and be disciplined."

It was asked: "What if the value of the slave is twenty thousand?"
Imam (as) replied: "The value of a slave cannot exceed the blood money (diyyah) of a free person."
